is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.s. populations (Page 1, Title).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) and L1014S (kdr-east) mutations (Page 2, Background; Table 3).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 3 (Page 8) provides allele frequencies and sample sizes (N) for multiple sites and years. Table 4 (Page 8) provides detailed genotype counts (RR/RS/SS) for survivors and dead mosquitoes.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from four sites in Southern Cameroon: Ipono, Bonanloka, Nkolondom, and Mangoum (Page 2, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article reporting original longitudinal data (Page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data are reported for four specific localities: Ipono, Bonanloka, Nkolondom, and Mangoum, with coordinates provided (Page 2, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in specific years: 2001, 2003, 2005, and 2007 (Page 3, Mosquito collections).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The authors mention previous cross-sectional surveys in the same sites (e.g., Etang et al. 2003, 2007; Reimer et al. 2008), but this paper presents a longitudinal analysis including new data points (Page 2, Background).

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype and bioassay data are contained within the main text and tables (Tables 2, 3, and 4).

assessment.summary: This study investigates the trends in insecticide resistance and the frequency of Vgsc L1014F and L1014S mutations in Anopheles gambiae s.s. (M and S molecular forms) in southern Cameroon. Collections were conducted between 2001 and 2007 across four sites representing urban and agro-industrial settings. The paper provides longitudinal genotype frequency data and correlates kdr genotypes with phenotypes (survivors vs. dead) from WHO susceptibility tests.
